goldens.comment: In .topic-meta-data h5 a, the original code had color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) but was changed to dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)). The lightness for the light theme changed from 30% to 70%, which is a dramatic inversion

This change for desktop/user.css changes $primary from 30% to 50% for the light theme; most other changes preserve the original $primary value and move the complement to $secondary for dark. Consider reviewing this (also applies to a similar .name change in the mobile variant).
In topic-post.css the original code used $lightness: 70% but the replacement uses $lightness: 30% for the light theme. This makes the text significantly darker than intended.

The light theme color for `.topic-meta-data h5 a` was changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`, which may unintentionally reduce contrast and affect readability. This change should be reviewed to ensure it aligns with design intentions.
In mobile/user.scss line 497, the lightness value for dark themes should be inverted to 70% instead of being changed to 50%. This change may lead to unintended visual regressions in light themes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/modal.scss:102 — The mobile message-length color reverses the expected 70% primary and 30% secondary mapping, producing wrong contrast in both themes.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for mobile/modal.scss line 102, the change is from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. This is indeed inconsistent with the pattern used throughout the rest of the diff, where typically 70% lightness on primary is paired with 30% lightness on secondary (e.g., in embed.css.scss, topic-post.scss, etc.). The finding correctly identifies that this specific change reverses the expected mapping - it uses 30% for primary and 70% for secondary, which is the opposite of the consistent pattern seen elsewhere in the diff. This would produce incorrect contrast.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/user.scss:522 — The group-member name changes from the existing 30% lightness to 50% in light themes and uses 50% rather than the intended 70% dark-theme inverse.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/user.scss around line 522, the change is from `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The finding correctly identifies that: 1) The light theme value changed from 30% to 50% lightness (a behavioral change, not just adding dark mode support), and 2) The dark theme uses 50% lightness on $secondary, whereas the pattern throughout the codebase for 30% $primary lightness is typically paired with 70% $secondary lightness (as seen in many other changes in this diff like line 119-125 in the same file). This appears to be an inconsistency/mistake in the conversion.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/modal.scss:102 — The custom-message counter reverses the required 70%/30% mapping, changing light-theme behavior and producing the wrong dark-theme value.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for mobile/modal.scss line 102, the change is from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. This is inconsistent with the pattern used throughout the rest of the diff. In all other cases, when converting from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: X%)`, the pattern is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: X%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 100-X%))`. For 70% lightness on primary, it should be 30% on secondary. But here, the values are swapped - 30% is used for primary (light theme) and 70% for secondary (dark theme), which reverses the expected behavior. This changes the light-theme appearance from 70% to 30% lightness, which is a significant visual change and likely a bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/topic-post.scss:182 — The topic-link heading changes from 20% to 50% in light themes and uses 50% rather than the intended 80% dark-theme inverse.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/topic-post.scss around line 179-182, the h3 color changes from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The finding correctly identifies that the light theme value changed from 20% to 50% lightness. However, for dark themes, using $secondary with 50% lightness is actually consistent with the pattern used throughout this diff (50% lightness on $secondary is common). The finding claims 80% should be the dark-theme inverse, but looking at other similar changes in the diff (e.g., line 30% primary -> 70% secondary), the pattern suggests 20% primary should map to 80% secondary, not 50%. So the dark theme value of 50% does appear inconsistent with the established pattern in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/common/admin/admin_base.scss:385 — The inverse primary/secondary lightness formula is duplicated across 109 declarations instead of centralized in a shared helper, making theme behavior prone to drift.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the diff introduces the same `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: X%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: Y%))` pattern across many files (109 declarations as claimed is plausible given the extensive diff). This is a legitimate architectural concern - the pattern is repeated verbatim throughout the codebase rather than being abstracted into a SCSS mixin or function. This creates maintenance burden and risk of inconsistency. However, this is not a bug - the code will work correctly. It's a valid code quality/architecture concern about the changes introduced in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/topic-post.scss:291 — No light-theme regression assertion covers this selector, allowing a dark-theme-only change to alter its existing primary lightness from 30% to 70%.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at line 291 in desktop/topic-post.scss, the diff shows changing from `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%);` to `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%));`. The finding claims this changes 'primary lightness from 30% to 70%' but this is intentional behavior - the dark-light-choose function selects the first argument (70% lightness of primary) for light themes and second argument (30% lightness of secondary) for dark themes. This is the consistent pattern used throughout the entire diff for dark theme support. The finding misunderstands that this is a deliberate design change to support dark themes, not a regression. The claim about 'no light-theme regression assertion' is about testing practices, not an actual bug in the code.
